pages.scan: Tier 1 left: caption 'Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown.' Ravi sits on a train with his chin on his hand, phone in his other hand. Tier 1 right: teal label 'WELBUK VISION'. Bottom caption: 'The vision: trusted connections between clinics, specialists, and patients across locations.' pages.observation: There are no speech balloons or tails on this page; it is all captions and labels. The reading order is clear: tier 1 left, then the top label and bottom caption of tier 1 right, then tier 2 (label, then caption), then tier 3 (top-right box, then bottom-left caption). Faces are clear in every panel. Overlaps: in tier 1 right the bottom caption covers the older doctor's lower torso and the stethoscope end, stopping just under his gesturing hand. In tier 2 the caption's right edge touches or covers part of Ravi's upper arm and shoulder, but not his pointing hand or the tablet. In tier 3 the top-right box touches Ravi's right shoulder area. The bottom-left caption covers the receptionist's lower legs and feet and touches the edge of the doctor's left leg. These are not faces, hands or key props, but the receptionist is visibly cropped by the caption in the final full-figure image. Confusing points: the woman in yellow and the boy in tier 2 have not appeared before and no text explains who they are; a reader will assume they are Ravi's family. The older doctor in tier 1 right is also new and unexplained. The shift from 'Tomorrow' and the train to the vision panels and then a group shot at the clinic reads as a closing montage. It is acceptable, but the timeline is loose.
